title: Max Makes It Right
author: Shellfie original
credit: An original story written for the McKinley Bulldogs.

pages: At recess, Max and a classmate named Theo both grab the same jump rope. "I had it first!" says Theo. "No, I did!" says Max. They pull and pull until the rope slips, and Theo falls down. Theo is not hurt, but Theo is very upset.

A teacher comes over. At McKinley, when there is a conflict, people talk it through so they can repair what happened. This is called a restorative conversation. The teacher takes Max and Theo to a quiet bench.

The teacher asks Max, "What happened?" Max explains, "We both wanted the rope, and I pulled too hard." Then the teacher asks, "What were you thinking about?" Max admits, "I was only thinking about winning."

Next, the teacher asks Theo, "How did this affect you?" Theo says, "I felt angry, and embarrassed when I fell in front of everyone." Max feels a heavy feeling in the stomach. Max did not want Theo to feel that way.

The last question is the most important one: "What can we do to make it right?" Max says, "I am sorry I pulled so hard. Next time, we can take turns." Theo thinks about it and nods. "You can go first tomorrow," Theo says.
The next day, Max and Theo turn the rope together for other kids. Max learned that making a mistake does not make you a bad Bulldog. Fixing it is what makes you a good one.

quiz.q: What did Max and Theo both want?
quiz.ev: Max and a classmate named Theo both grab the same jump rope.

quiz.q: Why did the teacher ask Theo how it affected him?
o: So Max could understand how Theo felt
